claims.claim: An arXiv paper finds that adjusting prediction-market prices by an implied settlement-discount curve reduces the near-certainty horizon gradient by roughly 48 to 88 percent.
claims.episode_span: Adjusting prices by those curves reduces the near-certainty horizon gradient by roughly 48 to 88 percent
claims.source_title: When Certainty Is Not Worth It: Capital Lock-Up and Settlement Discounting in Prediction Markets
claims.supporting_quote: Adjusting pricesby these curves reduces the near-certainty horizon gradient by roughly 48-88%, indicating that much of the raw maturity pattern reflects priced settlement frictions rather than forecast error alone.
